chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Every time this matter comes closer, the (need for) dissimulation (Taqiyya) intensifies.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Dissimulation or concealment of faith to avoid harm
key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter/event, specifically referring to the Rising of Al-Qaim

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the Rising of Al-Qaim and the practice of Taqiyya?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the dynamic nature of Taqiyya, indicating that as the occultation of the Imam and the approach of Al-Qaim's rising intensify political and social pressures, the necessity for concealment of faith becomes more pronounced. Shia scholars interpret this as a strategic adaptation to preserve the community's religious identity during periods of heightened persecution, reflecting the principle that the preservation of the self and faith takes precedence in times of danger. It serves as a reminder that religious obligations are not static but respond to the evolving historical and eschatological context.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Every time this matter (rising of Al-Qaimasws) comes closer, the (need for) dissimulation (Taqiyya) intensifies’.
en.sarwar: 17. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
As it (time of Imam al-Mahdi) draws closer, al-Taqiyyah will be more intensely needed.”
